subject: Archer API evidence ingestion: batch vs streaming
messages:

Subject: Question on Archer evidence ingestion options

Hi Michael / Neha,

We're getting ready to onboard our SOC 2 evidence into Archer and wanted to confirm the recommended ingestion pattern for a continuous sync. Our security team prefers an automated pipeline to avoid manual uploads each quarter. Two options were suggested by our internal infra folks:

- Bulk S3 drop with a manifest (objects pushed by CI)
- Archer streaming API that accepts per-evidence JSON payloads

Can you confirm which approach Redwood prefers for production (performance, supportability, rollback)? Also:
- Do you have a sample manifest schema we can mirror?
- Any guidance on object naming/partitioning for efficient search/CAIQ mapping?

We're aiming for a first ingest window the week of June 7. Attaching our current inventory export for reference (small sample).

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of IT Ops, Brightleaf Health
oliver.hayes@brightleafhealth.com

Subject: Re: Question on Archer evidence ingestion options

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear summary, this is exactly the right place to start. Looping in Archer onboarding so they can confirm specifics.

High level recommendation (based on what we've onboarded across customers):

1) S3 bulk drop + manifest (preferred for quarterly/periodic syncs)
   - Pros: simpler to implement from CI, easy to re-run/rollback, works well for large batches (many files)
   - Cons: introduces short latency until Archer picks up the drop; need to secure S3 role/policies

2) Streaming API (preferred for event-driven or near-real-time evidence flows)
   - Pros: low end-to-end latency, good for per-evidence updates (revocations, timestamp changes)
   - Cons: requires robust retry and idempotency handling on your side; slightly more engineering overhead initially

For Brightleaf Health's use case (periodic quarterly exports with occasional ad-hoc fixes), I suggest starting with S3 ingestion and switching to streaming later if you want real-time syncs.

I've attached a canonical CSV manifest we use (evidence_manifest_v2.csv) and a short S3 access instructions stub (s3_access_instructions.txt) — these show expected columns, object-key examples, and recommended partitioning by year/month/service. Archer onboarding: Natalie, can your team confirm the manifest columns below are acceptable and whether any additional mapping is required for CAIQ tags?

Sample manifest columns (first three):
- object_key, evidence_type, control_mapping, timestamp, checksum

Next steps:
- Oliver: confirm you can create an S3 bucket and provide an IAM role ARN or short-lived creds (we can also use pre-signed uploads)
- Archer: confirm ingestion job cadence (on-demand vs scheduled polling) and any maximum file-size limits
- We can schedule a 30-min sync early next week to align on mapping and run a test ingest

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on Archer evidence ingestion options

Hi all — thanks for the details. Confirming Archer supports both workflows. A few notes from our side: 

- S3 manifest: acceptable. Key requirements: object_key must be S3 URI (s3://bucket/path/to/file), each row should include evidence_type and control_id(s). Max manifest size: 250k rows per file; if larger split into chunks.
- API: we expose a /v1/evidence ingest endpoint with idempotency-key header. Rate limit: 1200 requests/min per account.
- We can do a one-time mapping where we map evidence_type -> CAIQ control IDs. If you share a sample manifest we will run a dry ingest in our staging env.

Attached: sample payload JSON (archer_ingest_payload_example.json) and our ingest doc: https://archersec.onboarding/ingest/BR-4821

If you want, we can start with S3. Provide an IAM role ARN with read access and we will kick off a validation job and produce a mapping report within 48 hours of receiving the manifest.

Regards,
Natalie Reed
Onboarding Manager, Archer Security
